title: Daniel and the Lions' Den
summary: When Babylon conquered Jerusalem, young Daniel and his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah — renamed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego — were taken to serve King Nebuchadnezzar. Daniel purposed in his heart not to defile himself with the king's food. He and his friends ate pulse and drank water, and after ten days they looked healthier than all the others. Later, Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and commanded everyone to bow to it. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refused, and they were thrown into a fiery furnace. The king saw four men walking in the fire, unharmed, and the three came out without even the smell of fire on them. Many years later, under King Darius, jealous officials tricked the king into signing a law that for thirty days no one could pray to any god or man except the king. Daniel went home, opened his windows toward Jerusalem, and prayed three times a day as he always had. He was thrown into the den of lions. In the morning the king hurried to the den, and Daniel answered: God had sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths. Darius then honored Daniel's God throughout his kingdom.

scriptures.text: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

characters.name: Daniel
characters.description: A young man from Judah taken to Babylon, who stayed faithful to God and prayed daily.

characters.name: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
characters.description: Daniel's friends, who refused to bow to the golden image and were saved in the fiery furnace.

characters.name: King Nebuchadnezzar
characters.description: The king of Babylon who set up the golden image.

characters.name: King Darius
characters.description: The king who was tricked into throwing Daniel to the lions, and who rejoiced when Daniel was saved.

lesson: Daniel's courage in the lions' den grew out of a daily habit of prayer. He decided ahead of time to be faithful in small things, so he was ready for the big test. We can be respectful to the people in authority over us and still put God first. God may not always rescue us the way He rescued Daniel, but He is always with us and always worthy of our trust.

reviewQuestions.question: What did Daniel and his friends eat instead of the king's food?
How many men did King Nebuchadnezzar see walking in the fiery furnace?
How many times a day did Daniel pray?
Which king had Daniel thrown into the lions' den?
Why didn't the lions hurt Daniel?
reviewQuestions.answer: God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths (Daniel 6:22).
